subject.title: fix(skills): require resolved approval before mutating actions

question: Should a fully specified user request with the exact destination, content, and action count as approval, or must every mutation receive a second resolved-preview confirmation?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes established guidance from conditional confirmation to unconditional second approval, trading lower accidental-action risk for additional user friction; automated checks cannot choose that security boundary.

options.title: Reapprove only resolved changes
options.body: Treat an exact recipient, content, and action request as approval, but require a new preview whenever lookup, substitution, attachment selection, fees, addresses, attendees, or other resolved details affect the action.

options.title: Always require second approval
options.body: Adopt the stricter rule for every mutation and explicitly accept the additional round trip even for fully specified requests.

options.title: Limit this PR to ambiguous flows
options.body: Land only the order, recipient-resolution, attachment, and file-selection hardening while leaving universal confirmation policy for separate discussion.

recommendation.title: Reapprove only resolved changes
recommendation.body: Treat an exact recipient, content, and action request as approval, but require a new preview whenever lookup, substitution, attachment selection, fees, addresses, attendees, or other resolved details affect the action.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the heavily owned `gog` and `ordercli` guidance and the upstream command semantics he maintains.
